candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Fort Worth output is qualified for defense-relevant customers using fully compliant non-Chinese feedstock, including heavy rare-earth inputs such as dysprosium and terbium.

candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as a benchmark to compare smaller or less obvious suppliers against actual qualification, feedstock origin, and downstream magnet milestones.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify customer names or sectors, DoD or defense-prime qualification milestones, production volumes, feedstock origin, heavy rare-earth availability, and whether announced government financing closes on stated terms.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Rare earth processing, metals, alloys and NdFeB magnet manufacturing
candidates.theme_relation: Potential second U.S.-listed mine-to-magnet / process-to-magnet platform exposed to defense sourcing policy, CHIPS/industrial funding, tariffs, and customer qualification cycles.

candidates.theme_relation: High-beta second-order exposure to government-backed reshoring of rare-earth refining, recycling, and domestic magnet inputs, but public-company linkage and scale need stricter verification.

evidence.claim: DoD awarded MP Materials $35 million to build U.S. heavy rare-earth separation capacity for HREE products used in DoD and civilian applications.
evidence.source_title: DoD Awards $35 Million to MP Materials to Build U.S. Heavy Rare Earth Separation Capacity

evidence.claim: MP Materials received a $58.5 million award to advance construction of its Fort Worth rare-earth magnet manufacturing facility and stated that raw material inputs would be sourced from Mountain Pass.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Awarded $58.5 Million to Advance U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Manufacturing

evidence.claim: USA Rare Earth announced commissioning of Phase 1a magnet production at its Stillwater facility and describes operations spanning heavy rare-earth processing, metal-making, alloy production, and neodymium magnet manufacturing.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth Achieves Major Operational and Strategic Milestone with Commissioning of Phase 1a Magnet Production at Stillwater Facility

evidence.claim: USA Rare Earth announced a partnership with Arnold Magnetic Technologies under which Arnold would offer USAR processed and refined NdFeB feedstock and finished magnets.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth and Arnold Magnetic Technologies Partner to Expand U.S.-Made Rare Earth Magnet Supply for Critical Industries

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels reports production of high-purity separated NdPr oxide at commercial scale from monazite feedstock at the White Mesa Mill.

Energy Fuels stated that NdPr oxide from U.S.-sourced monazite was manufactured into commercial-scale rare-earth permanent magnets, and that it signed an MOU with Vulcan Elements to advance an ex-China magnet supply chain.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels Announces 2025 Results and 2026 Guidance

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels announced that its U.S.-produced dysprosium oxide was qualified for use in permanent magnets, following earlier NdPr oxide qualification for NdFeB magnet applications.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels' US-Produced Heavy Rare Earth Oxide Successfully Qualified for Use in Permanent Magnets

evidence.claim: American Resources describes itself as a critical materials provider to rare-earth magnet, battery, semiconductor, defense and commercial supply chains, with domestic supply-chain exposure through ReElement Technologies.
ReElement states that its chromatographic platform can produce rare-earth oxides from mineral concentrates, recycled magnets, and magnet manufacturing waste.
Vulcan Elements announced a commercial-scale offtake agreement with ReElement Technologies to support domestic rare-earth magnet production.
evidence.source_title: Vulcan Elements Announces Commercial-Scale Offtake Agreement with ReElement Technologies to Enable Domestic Rare Earth Magnet Production

evidence.claim: The key investable bottleneck may be customer-qualified, compliant oxide-to-metal-to-magnet supply rather than headline non-Chinese mining or nominal magnet capacity.
evidence.source_title: Defense Critical Minerals Policy is Moving From Sourcing Restrictions to Supply Chain Requirements

evidence.claim: Defense supply chains often have poor subtier visibility, which supports looking for obscure lower-tier suppliers rather than only prime contractors or headline miners.

memory_update.text: MP should be retained as the reference anchor for U.S. mine-to-magnet integration, but it is not the primary underfollowed discovery target.
USAR is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the rare-earth magnet qualification node because it reports Stillwater magnet commissioning plus metal/alloy/feedstock capabilities.
UUUU should be tracked as a magnet-grade rare-earth oxide supplier rather than only as a uranium name; qualification of NdPr and Dy oxides is the key signal.
AREC/ReElement is a below-300m speculative exception; do not promote beyond Layer 1 unless SEC filings and customer/offtake evidence confirm scale, ownership economics, and qualification.

For this node, prioritize proof of compliant feedstock origin, heavy rare-earth availability, metal/alloy conversion, sintered NdFeB production, and customer qualification over generic rare-earth resource size.

Need a follow-up pass on non-US-listed but relevant comparables such as Neo Performance Materials, Lynas, private Vulcan Elements, Arnold Magnetic Technologies, and HyProMag to benchmark U.S.-listed candidates.

summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around a policy-driven rare-earth magnet qualification chokepoint. The scarce layer appears to be qualified oxide-to-metal-to-alloy-to-NdFeB magnet capacity that can document non-Chinese feedstock for defense and dual-use customers, not merely rare-earth mining tonnage. The two-lane list keeps MP Materials as the obvious reference anchor, then prioritizes USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels, and American Resources/ReElement as underfollowed or speculative public-market ways to track compliant feedstock, separation, magnet-grade oxides, recycling, and domestic magnet-chain qualification.
